pairs.subject: conflict-of-interest-detection
pairs.evidence: app/zakony/kolize/feed.xml/route.ts:25 The public RSS/JSON Kolizní-radar feeds publish a per-bill 'příznak střetu u předkladatele' entry carrying a summed contract CZK. The bill.flagged_conflict prop behind it is computed over every linked_to edge with no review/corroboration gate, no tie-class partition, no role-window test and no statute-relevance table, so the four-gate intersection the standard requires is skipped at a publication exit (the 'vyžaduje lidské ověření' copy in deriveRadar mitigates the framing but does not replace the gates).

techniques.evidence: app/zakony/kolize/feed.json/route.ts:26 Public exit. The flags come from kg-legislation-ingest.ts:61 (`if (e.rel === "linked_to") {`), which takes every tie. graph-schema.md says all 211 ties are pending_review and only some are registry-confirmed, yet review_state and corroboration are never read.

scripts/data-analysis/kg-legislation-ingest.ts:88 Builds one mixed total across all of a sponsor's linked companies with tie_class ignored. Steward seats are summed in with owner-operator money and shown as sponsorContractCzk in the published flag.

scripts/data-analysis/kg-legislation-ingest.ts:137 The flag condition is money-only. role_valid_from/to and temporal_status exist on the edges, but nothing tests the bill date against the role window.

scripts/data-analysis/kg-legislation-ingest.ts:135 Any bill a money-tied MP sponsors gets flagged whatever statutes it amends. There is no channel-to-statute table, so a public-procurement-money tie flags unrelated legislation.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard's four-gate intersection is written for vote-based joins. It could say explicitly that bill sponsorship (authoring or submitting a bill) is a decision act that the same gates (tie confirmed, window, statute relevance) must govern when it is published as a conflict flag.
